story.title: Alaska Attorneys Reject Trump's Request to Set Aside Senate Ballots as 'Meritless'
story.summary: Attorneys for Alaska have described Trump's demand to set aside Senate ballots as 'meritless' and 'not even possible.' This statement comes amid a broader investigation by the Department of Justice, which has issued subpoenas related to the case. Additionally, there is a request for a judge to separate ballots showing votes for a specific candidate until it can be determined if voters were misled into voting for a spoiler candidate.

explore_lenses.label: What changed in court on November 1?
explore_lenses.title: The federal case was dismissed before Election Day
explore_lenses.summary: On November 1, 2026, U.S. District Judge Sharon L. Gleason dismissed the Justice Department lawsuit that sought to block certification if Sen. Dan Sullivan lost. The dismissal means the requested federal pre-certification intervention will not proceed under this case before Alaska's November 3 election.

claims.text: Judge Gleason dismissed the Justice Department's lawsuit seeking to block certification of Alaska's Senate result if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan lost.
The suit had sought an unspecified investigation into whether Sen. Sullivan would have won absent alleged voter confusion caused by candidate Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.'s similar name.
Whether the Justice Department will appeal, alter its legal theory, or seek other election-related relief was not established in the reporting consulted.

explore_lenses.label: Why did Alaska call ballot segregation impossible?
explore_lenses.title: Ballot secrecy and commingled ballots were central
explore_lenses.summary: The Justice Department asked to preserve and segregate ballots ranking Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. while it investigated potential confusion. Alaska argued that election procedures made this infeasible without exposing individual voters' choices, and the judge accepted that the government had not supplied a workable secrecy-preserving method.

claims.text: The Justice Department asked the court to preserve and segregate ballots ranking Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. as part of its investigation of potential voter confusion.

Alaska's attorneys argued that ballots are commingled in ballot boxes and that separating ballots by candidate ranking could violate ballot secrecy; they described the request as 'disturbing and impossible.'
Judge Gleason said the proposed investigation was infeasible because early ballots had been mixed together and the government had not offered a workable process that preserved ballot secrecy.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about the alleged decoy-candidate effort?
explore_lenses.title: The candidate remained legally eligible, while allegations are investigated
explore_lenses.summary: The dispute concerns Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., who shares a surname and similar first name with incumbent Sen. Dan S. Sullivan. Alaska courts required that Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. remain on the ballot under state law, while allegations about why he entered the race remain contested and subject to investigations.

claims.text: Alaska's official candidate list identifies the two Senate candidates separately: incumbent Republican 'Sullivan, Dan S.' and undeclared 'Sullivan, Daniel J. Jr.'; it also lists Democrat Mary Peltola among the certified candidates.
The Alaska Supreme Court ruled in June that Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. met the legal requirements to remain on the ballot, after the Division of Elections had tried to remove him.

The Justice Department and Trump administration have treated the candidacy as a possible effort to confuse voters; Peltola has denied involvement in recruiting the second Sullivan, while the second Sullivan has said he ran independently.

Federal prosecutors confirmed a criminal investigation and issued subpoenas, but the consulted reporting did not identify criminal charges or a conclusive finding that any campaign illegally recruited Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.

story_report.summary: A federal judge dismissed the Justice Department’s effort to block certification of Alaska’s Senate result if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan lost, after state attorneys called the related ballot request meritless and impossible. The government had sought to preserve and segregate ballots ranking another candidate, Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., while examining possible voter confusion over the similar names. Judge Gleason found the proposed process infeasible. The immediate effect is that this request for pre-certification relief has been rejected, without resolving the election result or a separate criminal investigation.

sections.heading: Ballot Secrecy Blocks Segregation Request
sections.body: The Justice Department asked the court to preserve and separate ballots that ranked Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. as part of its inquiry into potential voter confusion. Alaska’s attorneys said ballots had been commingled in ballot boxes and argued that sorting them by candidate ranking could compromise ballot secrecy, describing the proposal as “disturbing and impossible.” Gleason concluded that early ballots had already been mixed and that the government had not supplied a workable secrecy-preserving procedure.

sections.heading: Sullivan Candidacy Remains Under Scrutiny
sections.body: Alaska’s official candidate list separately identifies incumbent Republican Dan S. Sullivan and undeclared candidate Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.; Democrat Mary Peltola is also listed. The Alaska Supreme Court ruled in June that Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. met the legal requirements to remain on the ballot after the Division of Elections sought to remove him. The Justice Department and Trump administration have treated his candidacy as possible voter confusion, while Peltola denies recruiting him and he says he ran independently.

unresolved.text: It is not established whether the Justice Department will appeal the dismissal, change its legal theory or pursue other election-related relief.

Federal prosecutors have confirmed a criminal investigation and issued subpoenas, but the reporting identifies no charges or final finding about whether anyone illegally organized Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.’s candidacy.

related_stories.title: Ciara Mageean, European Champion Runner, Dies at 34 After Cancer Battle
related_stories.summary: Ciara Mageean, the Irish Olympian and European 1,500m champion, has passed away at the age of 34 after a battle with cancer. Mageean, who represented Ireland in two Olympic Games, revealed her cancer diagnosis a year prior to her death. Tributes have been paid from various figures, including President Catherine Connolly.

related_stories.title: Record Early Voting Ahead of Upcoming Midterm Elections
related_stories.summary: As the midterm elections approach, over 50 million votes have already been cast, marking a record for early voting. This turnout surpasses the early voting figures from the 2022 midterm elections, indicating heightened engagement from voters as both parties ramp up their campaigns ahead of the polls on Tuesday.
